summary: Tigris & Euphrates is Knizia's abstract civilization classic where players place tiles to grow kingdoms led by four types of leaders, with your final score determined by your weakest of the four color categories, forcing balanced development. Conflicts between adjacent kingdoms are resolved by leader strength and can wipe out large swaths of tiles, making it a tense, cutthroat game beneath its calm exterior.
praised: brilliant 'your weakest category counts' scoring twist
deep, elegant rules with minimal luck
criticised: steep learning curve for an abstract game
can feel harsh or swingy for newer players when a kingdom collapses
dry presentation that undersells its depth

interaction.kind: tile placement leading to open conflict
interaction.detail: Tiles and leaders are placed on one shared grid, and when rival civilizations connect, external conflicts directly remove the losing player's leader or tiles from the board; internal conflicts can also unseat an opponent's leader. Tiles are drawn blind rather than from a visible market, so the interaction is entirely through spatial contact and combat, not a shared supply.

subsystems: single tile-placement/leader-network engine scored in four colors
scoring.how_you_win: You build interconnected civilizations by placing tiles and leaders, winning internal and external conflicts to keep control of kingdoms, which earns points in four colors (red temples, blue farms, green markets, black government); when the tile supply runs out, your final score is only your weakest color, so the highest 'worst color' among all players wins.
scoring.score_note: score is your weakest category count
